summary: Exact counting must determine every decimal position, and the accepted implementation visits each position once, so its linear bound matches the problem-level lower bound without a genuine slower principal strategy to benchmark.

optimality.argument: Any of the S decimal positions may independently equal the requested digit and change the result, so an exact solution must determine every position; repeated remainder and division inspect each position exactly once.

replacement_checks.evidence: If any decimal position were not determined, changing only that position to or from digit could change the required total without being detected, establishing Omega(S).
The accepted implementation removes one decimal position per loop iteration and performs constant work for it, establishing O(S) time.

The certificate regression compares both exact packaged sources with an independent string-count oracle over exhaustive singleton/digit pairs, deterministic random legal arrays, all requested digits, and maximum-length/value boundaries.
